stem:
The Pauling electronegativity values of elements can be used to predict the chemical properties of compounds.

Use the information in Table 1.1 to answer the following questions.

Table 1.1

| element | H | Li | C | O | S |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pauling electronegativity value | 2.1 | 1.0 | 2.5 | 3.5 | 2.6 |
| first ionisation energy/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | 1310 | 519 | 1090 | 1310 | 1000 |
| second ionisation energy/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ | - | 7300 | 2350 | 3390 | 2260 |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
O and S are in Group 16.

Explain the difference in the Pauling electronegativity values of O and S.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{LiH}$ is an ionic compound.

Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of $\text{LiH}$.

Include **all** electrons.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest the shape of a molecule of $\text{H}_2\text{S}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation that represents the first ionisation energy of H.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why there is no information given in Table 1.1 for the second ionisation energy of H.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Give the full electronic configuration of $\text{S}^{2+}(\text{g})$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{SO}_2$ with $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of $\text{SO}_2$ with $\text{NaOH}$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{CO}_2$ with $\text{Mg}(\text{OH})_2$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.2 by placing a tick (✓) to show which of the compounds have molecules with an overall dipole moment.

Table 1.2

| compound | $\text{O=C=O}$ | $\text{O=S=O}$ | $\text{S=C=S}$ | $\text{S=C=O}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| overall dipole moment |  |  |  |  |

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
At $150^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $103\text{ kPa}$, all of the compounds listed in Table 1.2 are gases.

Under these conditions, $0.284\text{ g}$ of one of the compounds occupies a volume of $127\text{ cm}^3$.

Use this information to calculate the $M_{\text{r}}$ of the compound. Hence, identify the compound from those given in Table 1.2.

Show your working.
